messages.subject: Adding new probability distributions
parts: Hi everyone, I've implemented (in C++) some circular probability distributions for my team and I would like to submit them for inclusion in stan/rstan. Can someone walk me through the process?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Adding new probability distributions
parts:
On Wednesday, September 19, 2012 11:06:57 AM UTC-4, Daniel Mitchell wrote:
Hi everyone, I've implemented (in C++) some circular probability distributions for my team and I would like to submit them for inclusion in stan/rstan. Can someone walk me through the process?

We should have a document outlining the process for contributions, but at the moment we don't. In general, if you are familiar with git, then the best thing is to point us to a branch or send a patchset to the list. But in cases like this where the contribution is an entirely new C++ file, like my_distribution.hpp, then it is fine to just attach the file to an email to this list.

Rough guidelines for adding a new distribution:

-- Look at a .hpp file for a similar distribution that is already in stan (somewhere under src/stan/prob/distributions ) and try to follow the same conventions. Some distributions accept vector inputs and for some distributions we supplement the auto-diff process with analytic derivatives, but this is not absolutely essential at the outset. In other words, a slow but correct log density is better than nothing.

-- In general, it is important that the density work both for fixed inputs (data) and parameter inputs. We use templates in C++ to handle these different cases, but sometimes there is a lot of somewhat obscure code going on to implement all this.

-- Try to also add some tests (look under test/prob/distributions and test/agrad/distributions for examples) that verify that the log density evaluates to something that matches an external algorithm (such as that in an R package)

-- Document the new density in the .tex files under src/docs/stan-reference/ .

-- The last step is to expose the new distribution to the parser so that it can be used in .stan files. This involves editing  src/stan/gm/function_signatures.hpp and maybe some other stuff. We can help you with this when you get to this step.

But, overall. anything you can do to get the process started is a step in the right direction and if the new density is in demand, someone will work with you to get it across the finish line.

Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Adding new probability distributions
parts:
I just sketched out a way for users to add
their own distribution code without having them
built into Stan. But it'll be a few revisions
before this is in the code base. Even after it
is, we're still happy to take donated code and
integrate it.

On 9/19/12 11:06 AM, Daniel Mitchell wrote:
> Hi everyone, I've implemented (in C++) some circular probability distributions

As we've discussed recently (I can't recall if
it was on stan-dev or stan-users), sampling
circular distributions are problematic for Hamiltonian
Monte Carlo (of which NUTS is an instance). The
issue is that the manifold of values (here the
circle) can't be projected continuously into R^N.

If you only need a data distribution

y ~ circular(theta)

where y is known, there's no problem. But if y
can be variable, there's an issue with projecting
the circle to R^N.

> for my team and I would like to submit
> them for inclusion in stan/rstan. Can someone walk me through the process?

We're rather light on process per se and I'm
not sure what you mean by "in C++". Are they
integrated into Stan already or is it just
an implementation of a density for double/int
args?

As to submission, you just need to go along with
the BSD license. We're going to have to figure out
whether we keep adding copyright holders. The
Eigen

If you want to see how our distributions are
written, look at the code. They're in:

src/stan/prob/distributions/...

The biggest issues are:

- no external dependencies other than Boost and
Eigen

- independent template parameters for each
scalar/vector/matrix argument (not int) in
order to support auto-dif

- error checking policies implemented a la Boost

- propto calculations via type traits

- google test unit tests of all of the above,
including auto-dif tests and value tests

- vectorization via expression templates, which you
can see in normal.hpp; this isn't mandatory, but
it makes models way faster

- cumulative distribution functions, which we'll need
for truncated models; also optional

If you're still interested after looking at the above,
drop us the code via e-mail: st...@mc-stan.org
Or we can add you to the stan-dev list where we
discuss this kind of thing.

I'm happy to look at unintegrated code or git
diffs and provide feedback.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Adding new probability distributions
parts:
Right. For example, if we have a tight von Mises distribution with
mean pi (or -pi) and very low (circular) variance, it's very unlikely
that we'll ever cross the valley separating -pi and pi, even though
they're right next to each other on the circular coordinate system.

Matt
